Citrus Tristeza Closterovirus (CTV) Virion Architecture

~2,000 nm × 11 nm

Transmission electron micrograph schematic of the long flexuous rod virion. Features a unique bipolar capsid morphology with major coat protein (CP / p25) along the filament body and minor coat protein (CPm / p27) forming the distinctive ~75 nm rattlesnake tail.

5' Rattlesnake Tail (CPm p27 + p65 + p61) 19.3 kb (+)ssRNA Genome 3' Major Filament (CP p25, ~95%)

Mosaic Recombination Architecture

NGSWO [PZ429909]

Discovery from South India (Nalgonda, Telangana): Sweet orange isolate NGSWO represents an authentic inter-genotypic chimeric recombinant between severe quick-decline VT (Major Parent) and mild decline T30 (Minor Parent).

Pan-India Lineage Clade Segregation

Phylogenetic segregation deduced from maximum likelihood (ML) inference across 118 Indian and global reference isolates:

I
Clade I: Severe Quick Decline (VT / B165)
Prevalent in Vidarbha (Maharashtra) and South India. Induces rapid decline in sweet orange on sour orange rootstocks.
II
Clade II: Inter-Genotypic Recombinants (VT × T30)
Includes Nalgonda recombinant (`NGSWO` [PZ429909]) and novel Assam Khasi mandarin recombinants (`PQ568311`–`PQ568327`).
III
Clade III: Severe Lineage (T36-like)
Characterized by extreme seedling yellows, inverse stem pitting, and stunted tree canopies in indicator limes.
IV
Clade IV: Stem Pitting & Mandarin Decline (K10 / Kpg3)
Endemic stem-pitting strain identified by Dr. K. K. Biswas; major cause of mandarin dieback across Northeast India and Vidarbha.
V
Clade V: Mild Asymptomatic / Slow Decline (T30)
Widely used for cross-protection studies; causes mild or negligible symptoms on commercial citrus scions.

Laboratory 60 — ACPV, ICAR-IARI

Molecular Plant Virology, Citrus Genomics & Diagnostic Surveillance

Laboratory 60 at the Advanced Centre for Plant Virology (ACPV), Division of Plant Pathology, ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), New Delhi, is India's premier academic research hub dedicated to closterovirus molecular genetics, vector-virus-host interactions, viral recombinant evolution, and molecular diagnostics of Citrus tristeza virus (CTV).

Historic Milestones & Contributions of Laboratory 60

Pan-India Molecular Epidemiology

Mapped CTV incidence and disease severity (PDI) across the Vidarbha mandarin belt (Maharashtra), Northeast hill tracts (Assam, Meghalaya), and South India (Telangana & Andhra Pradesh).

Discovery of Stem Pitting (K10) & Recombinants

Identified the indigenous severe stem-pitting lineage (K10/Kpg3), discovered inter-genotypic recombinant `NGSWO` (VT × T30), and published novel Khasi mandarin recombinants (`BHKM-6`).

Tri-Gene Diagnostic Suite for Quarantine Certification

Established robust multi-target diagnostic indexing assays across CP, p23, and RdRp genomic regions to safeguard national citrus budwood certification and quarantine indexing.

About CitrusTristezaDB & Methodology

Laboratory 60, Advanced Centre for Plant Virology, ICAR-IARI, New Delhi

Surveillance Mission & Scope

CitrusTristezaDB (CTV-IndiaAtlas v2.5) is an open-access, pan-India comparative genomics and epidemiological surveillance portal for Citrus tristeza virus (CTV; genus Closterovirus, family Closteroviridae). Developed by Laboratory 60 at the Advanced Centre for Plant Virology (ACPV), Division of Plant Pathology, ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), New Delhi – 110012, India.

Genomic Dataset & Methodology

The portal houses 118 curated sequences across Northeast India (Assam Khasi mandarin, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur), Central India (Vidarbha Nagpur mandarin belt), South India (Telangana & Andhra Pradesh), and North India. Genomic data encompasses three critical viral loci:

  • Coat Protein (CP / ORF 7 — 672 bp): Primary structural capsid gene for lineage segregation and RT-qPCR primer targeting.
  • p23 Silencing Suppressor (ORF 11 — 630 bp): RNAi silencing suppressor determinant governing pathogenicity and citrus seedling yellows decline.
  • Replication Polyprotein (ORF 1a — 504 bp): Diagnostic 5' region differentiating recombinant strains and lineage origins.
